scope: Complete ground truth for the nine supplied pages of the Building 615 archive excerpt: project and sheet metadata, all populated schedule and BAS matrix cells, all printed written control sequences and P&ID context, logical sensor roles, and excerpt limits. This is not ground truth for the missing 182 pages of the original 191-sheet set and does not invent plan-level equipment, zone, actuator, controller, terminal, or wiring quantities.
reading_notes: A schedule row, a P&ID/template row, a logical sensor role and an installed physical device are different quantities. The supplied archive excerpt does not support treating them as interchangeable.
M-601 has 32 marked equipment schedule rows. M-505 adds 16 duct-silencer-design rows and 17 external-static-pressure rows; all 65 source schedule rows and their cells are embedded in this record.

The 193 BAS matrix rows are retained exactly in 12 P&ID/template tables. Local numeric tags are unique only within their printed table. This record does not inflate them into a building-wide terminal count.
M-507 and M-508 are P&ID/point-list sheets without written sequences. M-509 is the printed written hydronic-sequence source; the sheets are not conflated.

Every supplied page was visually reviewed and independently captured by MuPDF and Poppler. Parser agreement corroborates bounded text/cells, while visual review establishes page disposition and limitations; neither process invents missing project facts.

requirement_audit.finding: The project, site, owner/agency, design firm as printed, contract number and Final Submittal issue are captured from every supplied title block. The repeated issue date is not relabeled as a revision date.
All nine supplied pages have independently corroborated sheet numbers and titles in the metadata ledger, with a complete visual finding for each page.

The supplied pages are schedules, details and control schematics. The ledger records no title-block scale, zero graphic scale bars and zero measurable length-scaled views; M-505 detail captions are retained as NOT TO SCALE where printed.
All M-601 marked equipment schedule rows are classified and all M-505 schedule rows are retained. No plan anchor or installed total is claimed because the archive excludes mechanical plans.

The composite schedules module embeds every populated M-505 and M-601 schedule table: 65 rows and 2,758 exact cells, including notes, blanks, performance, hydronic, electrical, dimensional and selection fields.

All 193 printed BAS matrix rows are retained with their literal flag columns and bounded source rows. Ownership is explicitly limited to its printed P&ID/template/system scope because there is no supplied installed-equipment/controller roster.

The embedded M-506, M-509, M-511 and M-512 components retain BACNET/BAS/GUI/HMI statements and disclose that transport, addressing, baud rate and controller model are not stated in the supplied excerpt.

All printed M-506, M-509, M-510, M-511 and M-512 written sequences are retained in bounded two-engine assertions; M-507/M-508 P&ID context explicitly records that those two sheets do not print written sequences.

Twenty-five logical sensor/control-input roles are indexed from the controls sources. The archive contains no plan or sensor schedule, so physical counts and zone mapping remain not stated rather than being inferred from templates.

The missing 182 sheets, absent plans, M-505/M-601 naming scope, combined unit-heater row, absent separate valve/actuator schedules, and P&ID-versus-written-sequence distinction are explicitly retained.
Each of the nine supplied pages has a saved full-page Poppler render and a complete visual-review finding. The review is page-complete for this supplied archive excerpt only.

Each component is rechecked against retained MuPDF and Poppler captures at build and validation time. Exact table cells and bounded text assertions are independently checked; the composite assembly only embeds verified authored modules.

statements.text: THE NEW AIR-COOLED CHILLER SHALL BE INSTALLED WITH A BACNET COMPATIBLE CONTROLLER THAT MODULATES REFRIGERANT FLOW FOR COOLING BASED ON A PRE-DEFINED CHILLED WATER SUPPLY TEMPERATURE SET POINT.
THERE IS A CALL FOR COOLING: DEFINED AS ANY CHILLED WATER VALVE OPEN MORE THAN 20% (ADJ.) FOR A PERIOD OF 5 MINS. (ADJ.).
AND OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE IS GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO 55°F (ADJ.).
TO PREVENT SHORT CYCLING, THE CHILLED WATER SYSTEM SHALL REMAIN ENABLED OR DISABLED FOR AT LEAST 30 MINUTES (ADJ.).
THE LEAD PUMP SHALL RUN WHEN THE CHILLER IS COMMANDED TO START. THE LEAD CHILLED WATER PUMP WILL ROTATE AFTER A RUNTIME OF 1 WEEK (ADJ.).
THE CHILLED WATER PUMP SHALL START IMMEDIATELY ON RECEIVING CHILLER START COMMAND TO PROVIDE FLOW FOR THE CHILLER.
THE CHILLED WATER PUMP SHALL DISABLE AFTER 15 MINUTES (ADJ.) OF RECEIVING THE CHILLER STOP COMMAND TO MAINTAIN FLOW UNTIL THE CHILLER SHUTS DOWN.
THE BAS SHALL BE ABLE TO HAVE TWO-WAY COMMUNICATION WITH THE CHILLER CONTROLLER AND MONITOR AND ADJUST CHILLED WATER SET POINT BASED ON THE RESET STRATEGY.

THE CONTROLLER SHALL MEASURE CHILLED WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE WITH A SEPARATE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SENSOR IN THE LOOP AND MODULATE THE CHILLED WATER PUMP ECM TO MAINTAIN ITS CHILLED WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT (ADJ.).
THE ECM MINIMUM SPEED SHALL NOT DROP BELOW THE SPEED CORRESPONDING WITH 5% ABOVE THE CHILLER MANUFACTURER’S RECOMMENDED MINIMUM CHILLED WATER FLOW.
BAS SHALL MONITOR ALL OF THE CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVES EVERY (5) FIVE MINUTES (ADJ.) AND USE THE MOST WIDE-OPEN COIL POSITION IN THE ENTIRE SYSTEM AS THE CRITICAL VALVE.
IF THE CRITICAL CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVE IS MORE THAN 90% OPEN (ADJ.), THEN INCREASE THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT BY 1 PSI (ADJ.).

IN THE EVENT THAT THE CRITICAL CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVE IS LESS THAN 80% OPEN (ADJ.), AND THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT HAS BEEN REDUCED TO THE MINIMUM ALLOWABLE SYSTEM LIMIT, THE CHILLED WATER BYPASS VALVE LOCATED AT THE END OF LOOP SHALL BE OPENED TO ENSURE ADEQUATE CHILLED FLOW IS DELIVERED TO THE CHILLER.
FREEZE PROTECTION: IF THERE IS NO CALL FOR COOLING, OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE IS BELOW 38°F. PROVIDE ALARM AND START CHILLED WATER PUMPS TO SEND WATER IS FLOWING THRU THE CHILLER.

CHILLER SHUTDOWN SEQUENCE: THE CHILLER WILL GO THROUGH A SHUTDOWN SEQUENCE IF CHILLER START CONDITIONS ARE NOT MET. THE CHILLER WILL DISABLE FIRST AFTER GOING THROUGH ITS INTERNAL SHUTDOWN PROCEDURE AND THE LEAD CHILLED WATER PUMP SHALL DISABLE AFTER A DELAY OF 15 MINS. (ADJ.)

THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM SHALL BE ENERGIZED AND CONTROLLED BY THE BUILDING BAS SYSTEM TO MAINTAIN A PRE-DEFINED HEATING WATER TEMPERATURE SETPOINT. ALL CONTROL POINTS ON THE I/O POINTS LIST SHALL BE MONITORED AND/OR CONTROLLED VIA THE BAS SYSTEM THROUGH THE HMI.
THERE IS A CALL FOR HEATING: DEFINED AS ANY HEATING WATER CONTROL VALVE OPEN MORE THAN 20% (ADJ.) FOR A PERIOD OF 5 MINS. (ADJ.).
OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE LESS THAN 65°F (ADJ.).

THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM ENABLE POINT SHALL HAVE THE CAPABILITY OF BEING COMMANDED AND/OR OVERRIDDEN FROM THE HMI BY THE USER. TO PREVENT SHORT CYCLING, THE BOILER SYSTEM SHALL REMAIN ENABLED OR DISABLED FOR 30 MINS.(ADJ.).

THE TWO HEATING WATER SYSTEM PUMPS SHALL OPERATE IN A LEAD/STANDBY FASHION, WITH ONLY ONE PUMP RUNNING AT A TIME. THE SYSTEM PUMP SHALL RUN ANY TIME A HEATING WATER CONTROL VALVE IS OPEN MORE THAN 20% (ADJ.) FOR A PERIOD OF 5 MINS. (ADJ.). THE MOST OPEN VALVE IN THE SYSTEM IS HENCEFORTH TERMED THE “CRITICAL CONTROL VALVE”.
ON FAILURE OF THE LEAD PUMP, THE STANDBY PUMP SHALL RUN AND THE LEAD PUMP SHALL TURN OFF. CONTROL SYSTEM SHALL DISPLAY A PUMP FAILURE ALARM FOR THE LEAD PUMP ON THE HMI.

FREEZE PROTECTION: THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM PUMPS SHALL RUN FOR FREEZE PROTECTION WHENEVER OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE IS LESS THAN 38°F (ADJUSTABLE). THE SYSTEM BYPASS CONTROL VALVE SHALL MODULATE OPEN AS REQUIRED TO ALLOW BOTH SYSTEM PUMPS TO RUN (AT 40% SPEED RESPECTIVELY) AS REQUIRED FOR CIRCULATION. THE CONTROL SYSTEM SHALL DISPLAY FREEZE ALARM ON THE HMI FOR THE TIME THIS SEQUENCE IS ON.

THE CONTROLLER SHALL MEASURE HEATING WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE WITH A SEPARATE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SENSOR IN THE LOOP AND MODULATE THE HEATING WATER PUMP ECM TO MAINTAIN ITS HEATING WATER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT.
THE ECM MINIMUM SPEED SHALL NOT DROP BELOW THE SPEED CORRESPONDING WITH 30% OF THE MAXIMUM HEATING WATER FLOW.
IF THE CRITICAL HEATING CONTROL VALVE IS MORE THAN 90% OPEN (ADJ.), THEN INCREASE THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT BY 1 PSI (ADJ.).

IN THE EVENT THAT THE CRITICAL HEATING WATER CONTROL VALVE IS LESS THAN 80% OPEN (ADJ.), AND THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SET POINT HAS BEEN REDUCED TO THE MINIMUM ALLOWABLE SYSTEM LIMIT, THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM BYPASS VALVE LOCATED AT THE END OF LOOP SHALL BE OPENED TO ENSURE ADEQUATE HEATING FLOW IS DELIVERED TO PROTECT THE PUMP MOTORS.

THE BOILER CIRCULATOR PUMPS SHALL BE CONSTANT SPEED AND CONTROLLED IN A LEAD/LAG FASHION. THE LEAD PUMP SHALL ROTATE WHEN ITS RUNTIME EXCEEDS ONE WEEK (ADJ.) OR WHEN THE LEAD PUMP FAILS. WHEN THERE IS A CALL FOR HEATING THE LEAD PUMP SHALL BE ENERGIZED.

THE BOILER SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH A BACNET COMPATIBLE STANDALONE BOILER SYSTEM CONTROLLER. THE CONTROLLER SHALL CONTROL ALL OPERATIONS AND ENERGY INPUT (MODULATE COMBUSTION) TO MAINTAIN THE HOT WATER SUPPLY TEMPERATURE SETPOINT. THE BOILER SYSTEM CONTROLLER SHALL BE INTERFACED TO THE BAS AND ALLOW MONITORING AND ADJUSTMENT OF SET POINTS.

WHENEVER THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM IS IN FREEZE PROTECTION MODE DUE TO LOW OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE, WATER SHALL FLOW THROUGH THE BOILER CONTINUOUSLY. IF THERE IS NO CALL FOR HEATING, BUT HEATING WATER TEMPERATURE DROPS BELOW 35°F (ADJ.), BOILER SHALL START AND INCREASE WATER TEMPERATURE TO 45°F (ADJ.)

CO SENSOR: THE CO SENSOR SHALL CONTINUOUSLY MONITOR CARBON MONOXIDE CONTENT INSIDE THE MECHANICAL ROOM AND SHALL BE INTERLOCKED WITH THE BAS SYSTEM AND IF A CO LEVEL OF MORE THAN 100 PPM IS DETECTED, IT SHALL ALARM THE BAS SYSTEM TO SHUTDOWN THE BURNER IN THE BOILER AND STOP COMBUSTION PROCESS IMMEDIATELY.

statements.text: THE FAN COIL UNIT WILL CONSIST OF CHILLED WATER COOLING COIL, HOT WATER HEATING COIL, INTEGRAL VARIABLE SPEED DIRECT DRIVE SUPPLY AIR FAN, RETURN AIR DAMPER, AND FILTER.
Start/stop bases: preset time-of-day occupancy schedule through the BAS; unoccupied setback/set-up; local zone-thermostat override; or manual/remote BAS override.
WHEN THE FAN COIL UNIT IS OFF, THE CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVE SHALL BE FULLY CLOSED TO FLOW THROUGH THE COIL.

WHEN THE FAN COIL UNIT IS ENERGIZED BY OCCUPANCY SCHEDULE, THE SUPPLY AIR FAN SHALL RUN CONTINUOUSLY. THE FAN SPEED SHALL MODULATE ACCORDING TO THE MANUFACTURER'S PREFERRED SEQUENCE TO MAINTAIN A SPACE TEMPERATURE OF 78°F (ADJ.) IN COOLING AND 68°F (ADJ.) IN HEATING.

COOLING: UNDER NORMAL OPERATING CONDITIONS THE AVERAGING TYPE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE SENSOR (LOCATED IN UNIT DISCHARGE) WILL, ACTING THROUGH THE CONTROLLER, MODULATE THE CHILLED WATER COIL TO MAINTAIN A SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE OF 55°F (ADJ.).

HEATING: UNDER NORMAL OPERATING CONDITIONS THE AVERAGING TYPE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE SENSOR (LOCATED IN UNIT DISCHARGE) WILL, ACTING THROUGH THE CONTROLLER, MODULATE THE HOT WATER COIL TO MAINTAIN A SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE OF 85°F (ADJ.).
During unoccupied cooling, BAS energizes the chilled-water coil above 85°F (ADJ.) and operates it until space temperature drops to 83°F (ADJ.); the return-air damper remains fully open.
An averaging-type manual-reset freezestat in the mixed-air section fully opens the chilled-water control valve at 38°F (ADJ.), alarms BAS, and requires manual reset before return to normal operation.
Emergency shutdown is hard wired into the supply-fan motor-control circuit. It shuts down the fan, alarms BAS, and fully closes all control dampers and hydronic control valves.
Only one coil—heating or cooling—may operate at a time, except in freeze-protection mode.
Supply-fan failure uses a current transformer: commanded on with no detected current alarms BAS.
High/low supply-air-temperature alarm monitors the averaging sensor in the unit discharge; thresholds are above 60°F (ADJ.) or below 45°F (ADJ.).
High and low supply-static-pressure switches in the unit discharge are hard wired to shut down the supply fan and alarm BAS at above 4 inches W.C. (ADJ.) or below 0.5 inches W.C. (ADJ.).
A return-air-duct smoke detector is hard wired to shut down the fan, with auxiliary notification to fire alarm and BAS.
A differential-pressure switch across the filter alarms at a 0.70-inch static-pressure high limit (ADJ.); condensate float-switch overflow is hard wired to shut down the fan and alarm BAS.

UNOCCUPIED SETUP CONTROL: THE FAN COIL UNIT SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH UNOCCUPIED SETUP AND UNOCCUPIED SETBACK TEMPERATURE CONTROLS. DURING UNOCCUPIED CONDITIONS, THE BAS SHALL ENERGIZE THE CHILLED WATER COIL IF ANY ZONE’S SPACE AIR TEMPERATURE RISES ABOVE 85°F (ADJ.) DURING UNOCCUPIED HOURS AND THE ZONE IS IN COOLING MODE. ONCE ENERGIZED, THE CHILLED WATER COIL SHALL OPERATE UNDER NORMAL CONDITIONS UNTIL SPACE TEMPERATURE DROPS TO 83°F (ADJ.) FOR UNOCCUPIED SETUP.
RETURN AIR DAMPER SHALL REMAIN FULLY OPEN TO ALLOW FLOW THROUGH THE FAN COIL UNIT.

FREEZE PROTECTION: AN AVERAGING TYPE MANUAL-RESET FREEZESTAT INSTALLED IN THE MIXED AIR SECTION OF THE FAN COIL UNIT SHALL FULLY OPEN THE CHILLED WATER CONTROL VALVE TO ALLOW FLOW THROUGH THE COIL SHOULD THE MIXED AIR TEMPERATURE DROP TO 38°F (ADJ.). THE FREEZESTAT SHALL SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS. A MANUAL RESET OF THE FREEZESTAT SHALL BE REQUIRED FOR THE FAN COIL UNIT TO RETURN TO NORMAL OPERATING CONDITION.

EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN: AN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN SWITCH SHALL BE HARD WIRED IN TO SUPPLY FAN MOTOR CONTROL CIRCUIT TO SHUT DOWN THE FAN AND SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS WHEN THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN SWITCH IS ACTIVATED. ALL CONTROL DAMPERS AND HYDRONIC CONTROL VALVES, REGARDLESS OF WHAT MODE THE UNIT IS IN, SHALL FULLY CLOSE WHEN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN HAS BEEN ACTIVATED.

THE BAS SHALL ALLOW OPERATION OF ONLY ONE COIL (EITHER HEATING OR COOLING) AT A TIME. UNDER NO CONDITION SHALL BOTH HEATING AND COOLING VALVES BE SIMULTANEOUSLY OPEN OTHER THAN WHEN THE UNIT IS IN FREEZE PROTECTION MODE.
SUPPLY FAN FAILURE: A CURRENT TRANSFORMER (CT) INSTALLED ON THE SUPPLY FAN CIRCUIT SHALL SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS IF THE FAN IS COMMANDED ON AND NO CURRENT IS DETECTED.

HIGH AND LOW SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE: THE BAS SHALL MONITOR THE AVERAGING TYPE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE INSTALLED IN THE UNIT DISCHARGE AND SENDS AN ALARM IF THE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE EXCEEDS 60°F (ADJ.) OR DROPS BELOW 45°F (ADJ.).

HIGH SUPPLY STATIC PRESSURE ALARM: AN ADJUSTABLE TYPE HIGH STATIC PRESSURE SWITCH, INSTALLED IN THE UNIT DISCHARGE SHALL BE HARD WIRED INTO SUPPLY FAN MOTOR CONTROL CIRCUIT TO SHUT DOWN THE SUPPLY FAN AND SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS WHEN THE SUPPLY AIR STATIC PRESSURE EXCEEDS 4” W.C. (ADJ.).

SMOKE DETECTOR ALARM: SMOKE DETECTOR LOCATED IN THE RETURN AIR DUCTWORK SHALL BE HARD WIRED INTO THE MOTOR CONTROL CIRCUIT TO SHUT DOWN THE FAN. AN AUXILIARY CONTACT WILL NOTIFY THE FIRE ALARM SYSTEM AND SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS.

CLOGGED FILTER ALARM: A DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SWITCH INSTALLED ACROSS THE FILTER SECTION WILL, THROUGH THE CONTROLLER, ACTIVATE AN ALARM WHEN THE FILTER PRESSURE LOSS EXCEEDS THE HIGH LIMIT SETPOINT OF 0.70 INCH STATIC PRESSURE (ADJ.).

CONDENSATE OVERFLOW ALARM: A CONDENSATE FLOAT SWITCH INSTALLED IN THE AHU CONDENSATE DRAIN SHALL BE HARD WIRED INTO THE MOTOR CONTROL CIRCUIT TO SHUT DOWN THE FAN. AN AUXILIARY CONTACT WILL NOTIFY AND SEND AN ALARM TO THE BAS.

statements.text: THE DOAS SHALL BE A PACKAGED UNIT WITH A SUPPLY FAN AND EXHAUST FAN.
THE DOAS SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH A VFD FOR THE SUPPLY FAN, AND A VFD FOR THE EXHAUST FAN.
THE DOAS SHALL BE CONTROLLED BY THE BAS AND REMAIN ENABLED AT ALL TIMES.
DURING UNOCCUPIED HOURS: THE DOAS SHALL RUN AT 30% OF ITS FULL LOAD AND PROVIDE A MINIMUM AMOUNT OF OA AT ALL TIMES.
DURING OCCUPIED HOURS: WHEN OCCUPANCY IS DETECTED FOR MORE THAN 5 MINUTES, THE DOAS SHALL RUN AT A FULL LOAD CONTINUOUSLY.
SUPPLY AND EXHAUST AIR VOLUME SHALL BE BASED ON THE FEEDBACK FROM AIR FLOW MEASURE STATIONS.
DOAS CONTROL: THE DOAS SYSTEM SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH A FACTORY FURNISHED ON-BOARD BACNET CONTROLLER. THE MANUFACTURER SHALL USE ITS PREFERRED SEQUENCE TO MEET THE FOLLOWING REQUIREMENTS:
IN COOLING, THE CONTROLLER SHALL MONITOR THE CHILLED WATER COIL LEAVING AIR TEMPERATURE AND MODULATE CHILLED WATER FLOW TO MAINTAIN THE CHILLED WATER COIL LEAVING AIR TEMPERATURE SET POINT OF 55°F.
IN HEATING, THE CONTROLLER SHALL MONITOR THE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE AND MODULATE THE HOT WATER COIL TO MAINTAIN THE SUPPLY AIR TEMPERATURE SETPOINT OF 70°F.
IN ECONOMIZER, THE UNIT SHALL RUN USING AN OUTSIDE AIR DRY-BULB BASED CONTROL STRATEGY.

SUPPLY AIR FAN: THE CONTROLLER SHALL MONITOR DUCT STATIC PRESSURE AND MODULATE SUPPLY AIR FLOW THROUGH THE VFD TO MAINTAIN DOWNSTREAM STATIC PRESSURE SET POINT. SENSOR LOCATION AND SETPOINT SHALL BE DETERMINED BY THE TAB FIRM.
EXHAUST AIR FAN: EXHAUST AIR SHALL MODULATE TO BE 200 CFM LESS THAN SUPPLY AIR TO MAINTAIN A POSITIVE STATIC PRESSURE FOR THE SPACE.

THE ONBOARD BACNET CONTROLLER SHALL COMMUNICATE WITH THE BAS TO ALLOW AT THE MINIMUM MONITORING AND CONTROL OF I/O POINTS LISTED HERE. THE SYSTEM SHALL BE ENABLED BY THE BAS. ALL CONTROL POINTS ON THE I/O POINTS LIST SHALL BE MONITORED AND CONTROLLED FROM THE GRAPHIC USER INTERFACE (GUI).
THE ONBOARD BACNET CONTROLLER SHALL TRANSMIT SYSTEM ALARMS TO THE GUI. THE ONBOARD CONTROLLER SHALL, AT A MINIMUM, TRACK ALARMS LISTED IN THE I/O POINTS LIST.
